title: Introduce contract-enforced RAG harness quickstart and lightweight stub generator
author: Maya Kline
release_notes: Adds a contract-enforced RAG quickstart and a small CLI stub generator to simplify authoring tool contracts and deterministic replay for CI. No breaking API changes.
description: Summary: Adds a compact quickstart that demonstrates an end-to-end retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) workflow where tool-calls are validated by a contract enforcer and exercises deterministic replay for CI. Motivation: teams often need reproducible agent/tool-calling tests and a minimal path from authoring a tool contract to running isolated local e2e checks. This quickstart bundles a tiny stub generator (stubgen) that emits contract-conforming tool stubs, a harness to run deterministic replay against saved traces, and a short guided tutorial plus telemetry probes to validate instrumentation. Changeset: quickstart scaffold, stubgen CLI (Python), contract schema examples (JSON Schema and proto-like contract), harness runner for replaying recorded tool interactions, lightweight telemetry probes that emit standard Redwood event shapes, CI workflow and smoke tests, and docs. Checklist: - [x] Quickstart README with step-by-step usage and example traces - [x] stubgen CLI to generate tool stubs from contract file - [x] deterministic replay harness with assertion hooks - [x] telemetry probe presets + sample dashboard link - [x] CI smoke workflow added and green - [x] minimal tests and lint fixes. Usage highlights: 1) Author a tool contract (contracts/example_email_tool.json). 2) Run stubgen to produce a local stub server that enforces the contract (stubgen --contract contracts/example_email_tool.json --out stubs/email_stub). 3) Start the replay harness with a saved trace to reproduce an agent session deterministically (harness/replay.py --trace traces/session-20260210.json --assertions assertions.yaml). 4) Telemetry probes auto-instrument the harness and emit events compatible with the Console ingest adapter. Design notes: - Contract enforcement is deliberately lightweight: validation focuses on input/output shapes and required side-effect annotations, not full runtime policy evaluation. - Stubgen creates fast, in-memory stubs suitable for CI; for production you should wire the same contract to a real adapter. - Replay harness supports time-mocking and deterministic RNG seeds so runs are reproducible in CI. - Telemetry probes emit a compact event envelope that matches Redwood Console shapes to simplify onboarding. Tests and CI: added unit tests for contract validation, integration smoke test that runs a one-step agent session against the generated stub, and a deterministic replay e2e that asserts tool-call ordering and outputs. All CI checks passed after one lint iteration. Backwards compatibility: no API changes; quickstart is additive configuration and tooling only. Rollout: shipped as a quickstart under quickstarts/contract-harness; docs updated and linked from the Quickstarts index. Follow-ups: document additional contract patterns (streaming tool responses), add a TypeScript stubgen port, and add an optional networked stub runner for multi-service scenarios.
